content.overview: BNS s. 1 — Short title, commencement and application.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Section 1 names the Sanhita, lets the Centre notify different commencement dates, and sets extra-territorial reach — every person for acts in India, Indian citizens abroad, and anyone targeting a computer resource in India.
In student language: BNS s. 1 is the rule on “Short title, commencement and application”. The section provides that (1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 1 exists so that “Short title, commencement and application” has a closed legal test in Chapter I — Preliminary. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Name, commencement, extra-territorial reach, the dictionary, and how the Sanhita is read — including common intention in s. 3(5).

The provision in detail
1. (1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita

(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India

(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India

(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by—

(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India;

(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be;

(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer resource located in India

(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any special or local law

Definitions and key terms
“offence” — every act committed outside India which, if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita Illustration A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India.

Essential ingredients
1. (1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
2. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita
3. (3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India
4. (4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India
5. (5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by—
6. (a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India;
7. (b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be;
8. (c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer resource located in India
9. (6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any special or local law

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 1 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Explanations
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 1 (Short title, commencement and application) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 1 (Short title, commencement and application), Chapter I — Preliminary.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
   (2) (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita
   (3) (3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India
   (4) (4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India
   (5) (5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by—
   (6) (a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India;
   (7) (b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be;
   (8) (c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer resource located in India
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 1 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Name, commencement, extra-territorial reach, the dictionary, and how the Sanhita is read — including common intention in s. 3(5).. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of BNS s.1 and distinguish title, commencement and territorial application.
Apply the India, extra-territorial, Indian-registered vessel/aircraft and India-targeting computer-resource rules to a problem.
Structure a 10-mark or 16-mark answer using the statutory sub-sections.
enhancement.definition: BNS s.1 is the preliminary provision dealing with the name of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, commencement, territorial application, specified extra-territorial application, and preservation of special/local laws and specified service-related laws.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminal jurisdiction must be anchored to the statutory basis for applying the Sanhita to the place, person, vessel or aircraft, or computer resource involved. The section should therefore be analysed by its separate sub-sections rather than treated as a single territorial rule.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: BNS s.1: Short title, commencement and application. Heading checked against India Code arrangement. Body not verified.
essentialIngredients: Identify the relevant sub-section of s.1.
For an offence within India, establish the territorial connection contemplated by s.1(3).
For extra-territorial application, identify the statutory basis under s.1(4) or s.1(5).
For s.1(5), test Indian citizenship, Indian-registered ship/aircraft, or an offence targeting a computer resource located in India.
Check s.1(6) and any applicable special or local law before concluding.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: For an exam answer, separate the provision into commencement, ordinary territorial operation, extra-territorial operation, specified categories of extra-territorial conduct, and saving clauses. A person’s location alone does not answer every jurisdiction question; the exact statutory limb and facts must be matched. For commencement questions, distinguish the enactment of the statute from the date on which the relevant provision came into force.
examples: A person physically commits an offence in India: begin with s.1(3).
An Indian citizen commits an offence outside India: examine s.1(5)(a), subject to the provision's requirements and other applicable law.
A person outside India commits an offence targeting a computer resource located in India: examine s.1(5)(c).
An offence occurs on an Indian-registered aircraft outside India: examine s.1(5)(b).

rows.left: Where did the act or omission occur?
rows.right: What statutory connection brings the foreign conduct within the Sanhita?
Identify the precise extra-territorial category and its facts.

enhancement.problemApplication: Use IRAC: Issue — whether BNS applies; Rule — identify the exact s.1 sub-section; Application — map location, nationality, registration or computer-resource target to that sub-section; Conclusion — state whether the statutory connection is established and identify any remaining jurisdictional issue.

examAnswerStructure.shortAnswer: Define s.1 and identify its five principal operational themes: title, commencement, territorial application, extra-territorial application and savings.
examAnswerStructure.tenMark: Introduction → s.1 structure → commencement → territorial rule → extra-territorial categories → one or two illustrations → saving clause → conclusion.
examAnswerStructure.sixteenMark: Introduction → statutory scheme with sub-section references → detailed territorial/extraterritorial analysis → computer-resource limb → commencement issue → savings/special laws → hypothetical application → concise conclusion.

keyTakeaways: Do not treat all foreign conduct as automatically covered.
For cyber facts, identify the computer resource located in India and the statutory targeting requirement.
